body:
Context entries now borrow the body from the fully validated current source and
move selected metadata into the response. They avoid a temporary full-body JSON
copy and another structured-metadata copy. The complete parser/domain checks,
original source versions, metadata fields, UTF-8 excerpts, order and exact budgets
remain. Twelve release pairs preserve full normalized output and all 960 selected
read/version/order/budget checks. Rich dense contexts repeat 1.0–1.4 ms median
savings; ordinary gains are negligible and tails vary. This is a small allocation
improvement, not a universal perceived-latency, p95 or process-RSS claim.

Eight context tests and the 471-test full gate pass. Normally paired Chromium/
WebKit protocol and all 14 editor scenarios pass in both engines. The existing
HTTPS app is rebuilt/restarted, preserving 81 prior resource versions, three pins,
preferences, certificate, instance/epoch and full CLI context; all 32 served assets
match. Owner card changes remain separate. Next profile complete large-view and
editor/startup interactions; broader performance, physical-device/platform and
release acceptance remain open. See progress/2026-10-01-context-entry-allocation.md.

metadata.summary: Build source-current context entries without a full body copy
